facts.statement: Corythoraptor was first described by Lü et al. in 2017.
facts.quote: authority: Lü et al., 2017

facts.statement: Corythoraptor lived during the late Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous in South China.
facts.quote: Corythoraptor () is a genus of oviraptorid dinosaur from the late Maastrichtian Nanxiong Formation of South China.

facts.statement: Corythoraptor possessed a tall crest on its head similar to that of a modern cassowary.
facts.quote: It bears a tall crest similar to that of the modern cassowary

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the crest may have been used for display and to detect lower-frequency sounds through resonance.
facts.quote: possibly had a similar functionality of display and resonance to detect lower-frequency sounds

facts.statement: The bones of Corythoraptor were heavily pneumatized, containing many air pockets like other oviraptorids.
facts.quote: Like other oviraptorids, the bones of Corythoraptor were heavily pneumatized with many air pockets.

facts.statement: Microanalysis of the bones indicates that the type specimen likely died at the age of 6 or 7 years.
facts.quote: Microanalysis of the bones indicates seasonal growth spurts, and the type specimen probably died at the age of 6 or 7

facts.statement: The type specimen of Corythoraptor reached a length of 1.6 meters.
facts.quote: The type specimen reached 1.6 m in length.

facts.statement: Oviraptorids, including Corythoraptor, may have lived in arid environments and eaten drought-resistant plants, nuts, and seeds.
facts.quote: Oviraptorids may have predominantly inhabited arid environments and ate xerophytic (drought-resistant) plants, nuts, and seeds.

facts.statement: Corythoraptor coexisted with six other oviraptorid genera, suggesting they may have partitioned food resources.
facts.quote: However, Corythoraptor coexisted with six other oviraptorid genera, and they may have all eaten different foods (niche partitioning).

facts.statement: Corythoraptor was described by Chinese paleontologist Lü Junchang and colleagues in 2017.
facts.quote: Corythoraptor was described by Chinese paleontologist Lü Junchang and colleagues in 2017.

facts.statement: The fossil was discovered in the Late Cretaceous Nanxiong Formation near the Ganzhou Railway Station in Jiangxi, South China.
facts.quote: It was discovered in the Late Cretaceous Nanxiong Formation near the Ganzhou Railway Station in Ganzhou, Jiangxi, in South China.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is currently housed at the Jinzhou Paleontological Museum in Liaoning Province.
facts.quote: The specimen is now kept at the Jinzhou Paleontological Museum in Jinzhou, Liaoning Province.

facts.statement: The genus name Corythoraptor refers to the distinct crest on the dinosaur's head.
facts.quote: The name Corythoraptor is in reference to the distinct crest on its head.

facts.statement: The crest had a bony shell casing approximately 2 millimeters thick, possibly covered in keratin.
facts.quote: Corythoraptor bore a tall crest on its head similar to that of the modern cassowary, with a 2 mm thick perhaps keratinous bony shell casing.

facts.statement: Corythoraptor was a toothless dinosaur.
facts.quote: Corythoraptor was toothless.

facts.statement: Pits on the snout suggest Corythoraptor had a keratinous beak similar to that of ornithomimids.
facts.quote: The lower part of the premaxillae (at the tip of the snout) features several irregularly distributed pits, which probably represent foramina which allowed blood vessels to flow, indicating a keratinous sheath (rhamphotheca) over a beak similar to ornithomimids.

facts.statement: Corythoraptor possessed 12 neck vertebrae.
facts.quote: Corythoraptor has 12 neck vertebrae.

facts.statement: The 6th and 11th neck vertebrae were the longest in Corythoraptor.
facts.quote: The 6th and 11th vertebrae are the longest.

facts.statement: The preserved left humerus makes up about 27% of the total arm length including the hand.
facts.quote: The left humerus is almost completely preserved, and makes up about 27% of the entire length of the arm, and 48% excluding the hand.

facts.statement: The ulna was slightly shorter than the humerus and constituted 26% of the total arm length including the hand.
facts.quote: The ulna is slightly shorter than the humerus and makes up 26% of the entire arm length including the hand

facts.statement: The first metacarpal, or thumb, was the shortest finger bone and slightly concave on its underside.
facts.quote: The first metacarpal bone (the thumb) is the shortest and is slightly concave on the underside.

facts.statement: The second metacarpal was 41% longer than the first and had a shaft diameter equal to 13% of its total length.
facts.quote: The second metacarpal bone is 41% longer than the first, and is moderately robust with the shaft diameter being 13% of the total length.

facts.statement: The first phalanx was the longest finger bone, measuring about 72% longer than the second metacarpal.
facts.quote: The phalanges (finger bones) are long and robust, the longest being the first phalanx about 72% longer than the second metacarpal

facts.statement: The claws were weakly curved and decreased in both size and curvature from the first to the third finger.
facts.quote: The unguals (claws) are weakly curved, and decrease in size and curvature from first to third finger.

facts.statement: The tibia was 19% longer than the femur and featured a pronounced cnemial crest along half its length.
facts.quote: The tibia is 19% longer than the femur, and features a pronounced cnemial crest running along half of its length.

facts.statement: The foot measured 29% of the total leg length.
facts.quote: The foot is 29% the length of the leg.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Corythoraptor in a clade with Huanansaurus and closely related to Citipati, Rinchenia, and Oviraptor.
facts.quote: Corythoraptor is an oviraptorid, and phylogenetic analysis recovers it in a clade with Huanansaurus, and closely related to Citipati, the Zamyn Khondt oviraptorid, Rinchenia, and Oviraptor.

facts.statement: Cau (2024) questioned the validity of Corythoraptor, suggesting it is a junior synonym of Banji based on shared skull characteristics.
facts.quote: The validity of Corythoraptor was called into question by Cau (2024), who considered it to be a junior synonym of the contemporary Banji due to them both sharing unique characteristics of the skull.

facts.statement: Hao and Xu (2026) proposed that Corythoraptor is a junior synonym of Huanansaurus.
facts.quote: In 2026, Hao and Xu considered Corythoraptor as a junior synonym of Huanansaurus instead.

facts.statement: Corythoraptor was likely an omnivore, a hypothesis supported by the presence of stomach stones in related species used to digest tough plant matter.
facts.quote: Caudipteryx was found with gastroliths (stomach stones) which some herbivores use to aid in digesting tough plant matter, which all may indicate oviraptorids were omnivorous.

facts.statement: Although shellfish consumption has been proposed for oviraptorids, the jaw structure of Corythoraptor was not well-suited for crushing shells, and the environment likely lacked sufficient shellfish.
facts.quote: It has also been proposed they ate shellfish, but the jaws do not appear to have been well-equipped to crush shells, and the arid environment probably did not sustain a high enough shellfish population.

facts.statement: Three distinct dark bands on the radius of the holotype indicate periods of arrested growth, suggesting Corythoraptor experienced seasonal growth spurts.
facts.quote: A portion of the radius bears 3 distinct dark bands which indicate periods of arrested growth, which points to seasonal growth spurts.

facts.statement: Corythoraptor reached about 1.6 meters in length at the time of its death, which is considered medium-sized for an oviraptorid.
facts.quote: At this point in its development, Corythoraptor reached about 1.6 m in length, which is medium-sized for an oviraptorid.

facts.statement: If the crest served as a mating display, it suggests Corythoraptor was sexually active before reaching its maximum size, with growth continuing for over 8 years.
facts.quote: If the crest did serve as a mating display, this would suggest Corythoraptor was sexually active before it finished growing, and that growth continued for more than 8 years.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the crest of Corythoraptor may have functioned as a resonator to detect low-frequency sounds from predators, prey, or mating calls.
facts.quote: In Corythoraptor, the latter may have been used to hear predators or prey items, or possibly to pick up low frequency mating calls as modern cassowaries do.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Corythoraptor could produce low-frequency sounds, as these are typically generated in the throat.
facts.quote: However, it is unclear if Corythoraptor was capable of producing low frequencies since these are produced in the throat.

facts.statement: An alternative hypothesis is that the crest served for visual display of social status or fitness, though this is less supported by comparisons to modern cassowaries where casques vary little.
facts.quote: It is also possible the crests were used for display, with larger and more ornamented casques equating to higher ranking in the group hierarchy or better fitness during mating season, but cassowary casques do not vary very much between individuals.

facts.statement: Corythoraptor lived during the late Cretaceous period, approximately 74 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 74 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The holotype of Corythoraptor was discovered in Ganzhou, Jiangxi province, southern China, within the Nanxiong Formation sediments near a train station.
facts.quote: Fue descubierto en Ganzhou, provincia de Jianxi, al sur de China, en sedimentos de la, Formación Nanxiong, cerca de una estación de tren.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, JPM-2015-001, is an almost complete skeleton of an individual aged seven to eight years, lacking distal tail vertebrae but including the skull and lower jaw.
facts.quote: El holotipo, JPM-2015-001, o espécimen tipo, es un esqueleto casi completo de un individuo de aproximadamente siete u ocho años, sin las vértebras caudales distales pero que consta de cráneo y mandíbula inferior.

facts.statement: The species Corythoraptor jacobsi was named in honor of the paleontologist Louis L. Jacobs.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, C. jacobsi fue nombrada en honor al paleontólogo Louis L. Jacobs.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses place Corythoraptor in the family Oviraptoridae, forming a clade with its closest relative Huanansaurus, as well as Citipati, Rinchenia, Oviraptor, and other close relatives.
facts.quote: Los análisis filogenéticos posicionan a Corythoraptor como un miembro de la familia Oviraptoridae, formando un clado con Huanansaurus que es su pariente más próximo, y Citipati, un taxón no identificado, Rinchenia, Oviraptor y otros parientes cercanos de ese mismo clado.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Corythoraptor spans the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Corythoraptor belongs to the subfamily Citipatinae within the family Oviraptoridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Citipatinae

facts.statement: The environment where Corythoraptor fossils were found was likely a lakeside setting.
facts.quote: The area was probably a lakeside environment.

facts.statement: The Ganzhou area is renowned for high oviraptorid diversity, having yielded egg clutches, skeletons, and fossils of six other genera including Huanansaurus and Ganzhousaurus.
facts.quote: Ganzhou is well renowned for its oviraptorid diversity, yielding oviraptorid egg clutches, skeletons, and six other genera: Banji, Jiangxisaurus, Nankangia, Ganzhousaurus, Huanansaurus, and Tongtianlong.

facts.statement: Like its relatives, Corythoraptor had feathers, small wings, and a toothless beak.
facts.quote: Al igual que sus parientes tenía plumas, además de poseer pequeñas alas y un pico no dentado.

facts.statement: Corythoraptor possessed a very distinctive crest different from other oviraptorids, which is compared to that of the modern cassowary.
facts.quote: Tenía una cresta muy característica, diferente a la de otros ovirraptóridos, la cual se compara a la del actual casuario.

facts.statement: The crest and other skull characteristics distinguish Corythoraptor from its closest relative, Huanansaurus.
facts.quote: Dicha cresta y otras características del cráneo lo diferencian de su pariente más cercano, Huanansaurus.

facts.statement: The presence of six oviraptorid species in Ganzhou suggests they may have exhibited niche partitioning, targeting different food sources.
facts.quote: Because six different oviraptorid species are known from Ganzhou, they may have exhibited niche partitioning, with different species targeting different foods.
